title: Maximum Element After Decreasing and Rearranging
summary: Given an array of positive integers arr, you can perform operations to decrease any element to a smaller positive integer or rearrange the elements in any order.
statement: Given an array of positive integers arr, you can perform operations to decrease any element to a smaller positive integer or rearrange the elements in any order. The goal is to ensure the first element is 1 and the absolute difference between any two adjacent elements is at most 1. Determine the maximum possible value that any element in the array can achieve after performing these operations.
constraints: You may reorder freely and decrease values while keeping them positive.
Afterward the first value must be one and adjacent differences at most one; maximize the largest value.
hints: Small values are the bottleneck for building a gradual sequence.
Sort ascending and maintain the greatest feasible current endpoint.
For each value, set current=min(value,current+1), starting from zero.
The next endpoint cannot exceed either its original value or one above the prior endpoint; sorting ensures this locally maximal choice cannot reduce future options.
editorial: The next endpoint cannot exceed either its original value or one above the prior endpoint; sorting ensures this locally maximal choice cannot reduce future options.

tests.explanation: After sorting, the feasible sequence reaches maximum two.
Reorder and decrease to [1,2,3], reaching maximum three.
